segments.he: שֶׁלֹּא לְדַעַת — לְאֵיתוֹיֵי מֵסִיחַ לְפִי תוּמּוֹ.
segments.en: The Gemara further inquires: What is added by the phrase in the second part of the principle: If the blemish was caused «without» his «intent,» the animal’s slaughter is permitted? This serves «to add» an instance where a gentile did not inquire about the nature of the firstborn offering, but rather discovered it from one who «speaks offhandedly.» Although the gentile intentionally caused a blemish in the animal, since the Jew did not intentionally prompt him to cause it, the animal is permitted.

positions.claim: a blemish a gentile made after an offhand remark is permitted
